fields.jld\n\n 2024-05-15 15:39\n\nreporter:
I have reproduced this behavior using the supplied test file using gramps running from current (as of 2024-05-15) source.
This issue is (currently) not a failure to interpret the CAL gedcom tag as the Calculated quality, but rather the gedcom importer not parsing the tag without its being all-uppercase.
If the line "Cal 1847" is replaced with "CAL 1847" then the file is imported correctly, and when the person Franz Somebody is examined, the birth date is displayed correctly with the qualifier "Calculated."
The "Abt" line in the same test gedcom is not affected in the same way, because tags like ABT are parsed along with the text by the internal date parser, rather than being interpreted separately from the date text as CAL is.
It's possible that the situation is different from what it was in 2015, of course, but I believe that the above describes the current situation accurately.
It's not difficult to make the import of CAL to be case-insensitive, but the GEDCOM spec seems (to me) to say that tags should always be uppercase.
My opinion is that the ideal thing to do here would be to detect all tags that aren't in uppercase, and signal an error to the user. Of course, we're currently ignoring many (or all) of these, so this would break gramps for many users that import from poorly-formatted gedcom files. Perhaps it's still worth catching bad tags and warning the user about them (without stopping the import).
